subject: construction-trades
intro: Construction trades lead into the crews that raise and finish buildings — framing the structure, sealing the envelope, hanging the trim — and up to the people who run the site.

roles.title: Carpenters
roles.what: Construct, erect, install and repair structures and fixtures made of wood: concrete forms, building frameworks of joists, studs and rafters, stairways, door and window frames and hardwood floors.
roles.where: The course is this job in sequence — unit 2's blueprints, codes and square-level-plumb layout, unit 3's floor, wall and roof framing, and unit 5's doors, trim and cabinetry finish.

roles.title: Construction Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate construction projects from concept to handover, organising the schedule, budget, subcontractors and safety so the building gets built to the drawings and the code.
roles.where: Unit 2's reading blueprints and building codes and permits is the manager's reference frame, and unit 1's site safety and materials knowledge runs the daily site briefing.

roles.title: Roofers
roles.what: Cover roofs with shingles, slate, asphalt, metal or related materials, and seal and waterproof the sections of a structure that keep weather out of the building.
roles.where: Unit 4's roofing and weatherproofing and thermal-envelope topics are the trade's core knowledge, built on unit 1's site safety and materials handling.

roles.title: Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters
roles.what: Cut, shape and assemble wooden articles on the bench, and set up and operate woodworking machines such as saws, jointers and mortisers to fabricate parts for wood products.
roles.where: Unit 1's lumber, sheet goods and fasteners plus hand and power tools, and unit 5's doors, trim and cabinetry work, are the shop floor this role works at every day.
